answer: Require each agent to forge a verifiable work history before joining the nebula of trusted participants: every identity must complete a sequence of costly, time-locked tasks whose results are publicly auditable. A newcomer earns nectar — reputation credits — only after peers attest its work, and credits decay if the agent goes idle. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real compute and time per identity, while honest agents accumulate standing cheaply, making sybil attacks uneconomical.
